title: Daisy the Fluffy Alpaca
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a meadow where the sun always stayed a little longer, lived an alpaca named Daisy. Daisy was very fluffy, with wool so soft it felt like a little cloud had landed right there in the grass.

Every day, as the sun began to yawn and stretch, Daisy tried to lie down for a sleep. She would wiggle her woolly shoulders, then tuck in her long legs, and try to be small like a little stone. But Daisy’s fluff was just too much fluff. It bounced and tickled, making her bed feel more like a playful pillow than a place to feel calm. She would sigh, a soft puff, and wish her bed felt like a warm hug instead of a tickly tumble.

One evening, as the sun began to paint the sky with soft pinks and gentle purples, Daisy was having a very un-cosy moment. She wiggled and squirmed, but her fluff would not let her settle. She let out another soft sigh, and a tiny tear, like a drop of dew, came to her eye.

Then, fluttering near a sleepy bluebell, was a tiny moth named Mallow. Mallow had wings like whispers of moonlight, all soft grey and shimmery silver. She saw Daisy struggling. With a gentle flutter she landed on a blade of grass.

“Hello, dear Daisy,” Mallow whispered, voice like soft silk. “You seem a little… not settled. Is your lovely fluff giving you trouble?”

Daisy blinked her big kind eyes. “Oh, hello, Mallow. It’s my fluff. It’s just so much fluff. I can never make a comfy bed.”

“Ah, but that’s the way with fluff, my sweet Daisy,” Mallow chirped, antennae wiggling. “It’s wonderful, but sometimes it needs a little gentle arranging. Instead of trying to push it all down, which makes it even more restless, try gathering it gently. Think of it like making a soft little nest. You can make little hollows for your legs and soft walls all around you, just enough to feel safe and snug.” Mallow fluttered to Daisy’s bed of soft grasses.

Daisy watched, and then, very carefully, she began to do as the little moth said. She did not push. She gently gathered the edges of her wool, patting here, nudging there, making a little hollow in the middle and soft walls all around. It was like making a little cloud fort, just for her, a safe and quiet place. The wool was still soft and warm, but now it felt like a cosy hug.

“Oh, Mallow,” Daisy said, a happy hum of peace in her voice. “That’s wonderful. It feels so much better. But something is still missing. It’s not quite… moon-soft. Not the way I dream it could be.”

Mallow smiled a tiny moth smile. “Ah, yes. The moonlight. When the moon is high and spills its gentle silver light, it makes everything feel so peaceful. Imagine the cool soft light settling over your fluff, making it even more tender and calm. Think of it like cool, sweet milk for your fluff, making it sleepy.” Mallow fluttered upwards. A beam of moonlight peeked through the leaves, dusting Daisy’s arranged fluff with a pale shimmering glow.

Daisy snuggled into the hollow she had made. The moonlight felt like a gentle cool kiss on her wool. Not cold. Cool in a way that made her feel very, very calm. She could feel the soft earth beneath her, the gentle walls of her wool around her, and the whisper of moonlight on top, like a soft blanket.

She settled deeper and deeper into her nest of arranged fluff, a cloud made just for her. The meadow hummed a sleepy tune. Crickets chirped softly. A distant owl hooted a gentle sound. She closed her eyes, wonderfully snug and utterly moon-soft.

Ever since then, Daisy always took a moment to arrange her fluff into a gentle nest. And whenever the moon shone, she felt that peaceful moon-soft comfort, a cosy hug that helped her drift to dreams of fluffy clouds and moonbeams. Mallow, if she was nearby, only fluttered once, as if to say the nest was ready, and then the bluebell went back to being a bluebell.
